title: SpaceX scrubs launch of classified payload for the U.S. Space Force, targets Friday
html:
SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket stands at Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base ahead of the launch of the USSF-317 mission. Image: SpaceX

Update Nov. 19, 10:16 p.m. EDT (0316 UTC): SpaceX scrubbed the Thursday night launch attempt and is targeting Friday.

SpaceX plans to launch an undisclosed number of satellites on a Falcon 9 rocket on behalf of the U.S. Space Force on Friday night. SpaceX scrubbed the launch Thursday night, but didn’t state the reason why.

The mission, designated USSF-317, will fly from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg Space Force Base during a window that opens at 6:32 p.m. PST (9:32 p.m. EST / 0232 UTC). The rocket will fly on a south-easterly trajectory upon leaving the pad.

Spaceflight Now will have live coverage beginning about 30 minutes prior to liftoff.

This is the latest in a series of ‘R’ missions assigned to SpaceX. So far, there have been five previous such missions which include:

  • Aug. 16 – USSF-366 (R-1)
  • Sep. 10 – USSF-153 (R-2)
  • Sep. 26 – USSF-385 (R-3)
  • Nov. 06 – USSF-432 (R-4)
  • Nov. 12 – USSF-627 (R-5)

Following each of these launches, 23 satellites have been catalogued. To date, the U.S. Space Force hasn’t confirmed details about these satellites and has not made statements following these launches to confirm successful deployments.

SpaceX will launch the USSF-317 mission using the Falcon 9 first stage booster with the tail number B1100. This will be its 11th flight following the launches a NROL-105-, USSF-385, and eight batches of Starlink satellites.

A little more than eight minutes after liftoff, B1100 will target a landing on the droneship, Of Course I Still Love You. If successful, this will be the 235th landing on this vessel and the 679th Falcon booster landing to date.

SpaceX is scheduled to launch at least two more missions for the U.S. Space Force before the end of the month.
summary: The mission is the latest in the series of ‘R’ missions tasked by the U.S. Space Force. Liftoff from pad 4 East is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 20, during a window that opens at 6:32 p.m. PST (9:32 p.m. EST / 0232 UTC).
